Elodie (oncall): noticing a sudden spike in GPU attach latency in us-west3, lots of pods stuck at Attaching >90s. kubelet logs show device busy and long waiters :frowning:
Marco (storage): pulling nvme stats now. p50 io-latency jumped and qdepth collapsed on a narrow set of hosts tagged `scratch-exp`. looks like heavy background TRIM/GC activity coincident with the attach wave
Sasha (sre): did we roll anything that touches cleaner/trim behavior? we had an experimental async-TRIM rollout earlier today right?
Kai (infra): yes—we rolled async-trim v2 to 20% of nodes to reduce foreground fsync stalls. rollout targeted `scratch-exp` cohort at 04:00 UTC. patch notes said it batches TRIMs but keeps sync fallback for small writes
Marco (storage): logs show the rollout induced a degenerate path: the async batcher accumulates many small deletions and issues a single large batch which vendors' firmware treat as high-priority sync work, blocking other queues. vendor drives then serialized GC -> qdepth->1
Elodie (oncall): ugh. that's precisely what bites us during scale-up. immediate mitigation options?
trim-rollout-bot: rolling back async-trim v2 on nodes with label `scratch-exp` now. rollback started at 04:12:05 UTC. :gear:
Sasha (sre): while rollback proceeds, do two things: 1) bump nodepool ioQuota for `us-west3-gpu` to 2x to give kubelet headroom 2) temporarily raise kubelet attach timeout to avoid flapping
Elodie (oncall): applying ioQuota patch: `kubectl patch nodepool us-west3-gpu --patch '{"spec":{"ioQuota":"2x"}}'`. Patching kubelet-configmap to extend attach timeout by 30s
metrics-bot: host-local-io-latency p50 went 4ms -> 210ms at 04:11:; device-qdepth median collapsed 128->2; attach_pending peaked 37
Kai (infra): rollback completed on ~85% of targeted nodes, trim-rollout-bot reports leftovers being drained. also cordoning the top 3 affected nodes from new scheduling until qdepth stabilizes
Marco (storage): vendor note: certain controller firmware versions escalate large TRIM batches into synchronous remaps when concurrent sync fsyncs are present — effectively starving foreground IO. we'll open a vendor SR but need a short-term software fix
Sasha (sre): short-term software patch: make the async-trim batcher respect a max-batch-size and insert inter-batch sleeps; also add an attach-aware guard: if attach_pending>6 then defer batches. Kai, can you gate that as a hotfix flag?
Kai (infra): pushing feature-flag patch to ops-config: `asyncTrim.maxBatch=4k` and `asyncTrim.deferIfAttach>6`. will roll to 100% for `scratch-exp` after testing on a canary
trim-rollout-bot: feature-flag applied to canary nodes. running a small smoke test of attach / trim interplay. :test_tube:
Elodie (oncall): after rollback + ioQuota bump + cordons, attach backlog cleared in ~7m. keeping 30m watch. thanks all :relieved:
Marco (storage): long-term proposals: 1) avoid monolithic TRIM batches — prefer spread-out micro-batches 2) make cleaner/scrub replication-aware and attach-aware 3) add firmware/driver heuristics to downgrade TRIM priority under high attach load 4) schedule aggressive GC windows away from known provisioning waves
Sasha (sre): runbook addition: if async-trim rollout causes attach_pending>8 -> auto-rollback + ioQuota bump + page storage oncall. also add a perf test in CI that reproduces TRIM-batch + attach mix to catch regressions
Elodie (oncall): filing ticket INF-2026-ASYNC-TRIM-REGRESS with RCA notes and cost/availability blurb: rolling back trims trades immediate background cleanup (higher temporary write amplification/wear) for preserving provisioning SLA. will include vendor SR number once open
Kai (infra): also proposing a small billing note: if we keep ioQuota permanently higher for sensitive pools it increases cloud EBS/IOPS spend slightly; ops should quantify before permanent changes
Marco (storage): noted. will follow up on vendor SR and add firmware-aware test vectors. good catch everyone.
Elodie (oncall): thanks — I'll update channel if anything reappears.
